item.title: Treaty Day celebrates relationship with PEI Mi’kmaq
item.description:
Treaty Day celebrates relationship with PEI Mi’kmaq jenniferdhogan Thu, 10/01/2026 - 13:46

Today, Prince Edward Island recognizes Treaty Day to celebrate the relationship between the PEI Mi’kmaq and Islanders and reaffirm the province’s commitment to reconciliation.

Treaty Day also marks the beginning of Mi’kmaw History Month, a time to learn more about Mi’kmaq culture, language and traditions. The leadership of Abegweit First Nation and Lennox Island First Nation joined Premier Rob Lantz today at the Provincial Administration Building to raise the Mi’kmaq Grand Council flag, which will fly throughout October.

The province continues to work with Mi’kmaq partners to advance reconciliation and create opportunities for Indigenous Peoples and communities. Developing and maintaining strong, respectful partnerships with First Nation communities and Indigenous organizations is central to this work. 

This year, the provincial government renewed a four-year, $1.67 million agreement between SkillsPEI and the Mi’kmaq Confederacy of PEI to support Indigenous participants through employment programs, mentorship opportunities and essential workplace skills training.  

The province also continues to provide funding to help address systemic challenges through collaboration and partnership. This funding supports community-based programs and local initiatives that address MMIWG and gender-based violence, while promoting healing, cultural activities, and community connection. 

Throughout Mi’kmaw History Month, Islanders are encouraged to participate in events and learn more. The Indigenous Relations Secretariat will offer a lunch and learn series to the public service to help educate employees about the history, culture, and language of Mi’kmaq people.

Quotes: 

“The Peace and Friendship Treaties are the bedrock of coexistence in Epekwitk. Coming together as one community to celebrate more than 300 years of shared history is so important. It reminds us that we have grown together and overcome countless challenges as neighbours. While the path that brought us here has not always been smooth, it is our duty, as Treaty People, to continue the journey. Treaty Day reminds us to strive to build a better future for those still to come.”  

-Lennox Island First Nation Chief Tabatha Bernard

“Treaty Day commemorates the Peace and Friendship Treaties signed by our ancestors, but for me it is also a celebration of the future. Our ancestors signed the Treaties hoping for a better future built on understanding and acceptance. The Treaties are about two nations finding a way to work together for their mutual benefit. In that way, we are all Treaty People, and that gives me hope for our future.”   

- Abegweit First Nation Chief Junior Gould  

“Treaty Day is an opportunity to celebrate the relationship we share with the PEI Mi’kmaq and to reflect on our shared responsibility to continue the work of reconciliation. That work is built on respect, understanding and meaningful collaboration. As Mi’kmaw History Month begins, I encourage Islanders to learn more about Mi’kmaq history, culture and traditions, and to take part in opportunities throughout the month to listen, learn and come together.”  

-Premier Rob Lantz

L’nuey is holding a Mawi’omi at the Eastlink Centre today (October 1) from 10:30 a.m. to 3 p.m. to commemorate the historic Peace and Friendship Treaties and the unique relationship between the Mi’kmaq and the Crown. 

Visit Understanding Indigenous Matters and L’nuey to learn more about reconciliation.

item.title: Statement by Minister Ramsay on National Seniors Day
item.description:
Statement by Minister Ramsay on National Seniors Day jenniferdhogan Thu, 10/01/2026 - 10:14

Minister of Social Development and Seniors Barb Ramsay issued the following statement: 

“Today is National Seniors Day, a time to celebrate older adults and thank them for the countless contributions they make to our province.

Earlier this year, our department launched the Seniors Action Plan for 2026-2031. I encourage you to take the opportunity to review the plan and see how we are working with partners and communities to help seniors thrive. The plan builds on the significant progress that has already been made to support seniors, while introducing new strategies and actions that address the current and future needs and priorities of island seniors. 

The priorities in the Seniors Action Plan are reflected in the programs that we continue to invest in across the province. Recently, we announced Seniors Community Meal Grants and Seniors’ Secretariat Grants, which help support community connections and enhance the quality of life for seniors. Tomorrow, we will be recognizing older adults with the 2026 Senior Islander of the Year Award.

Improving the aging experience is a top priority for our department, but we also know it is a shared responsibility. By supporting older adults, we strengthen the social and economic fabric of our province. Today, and throughout the year, I encourage Islanders to reach out and connect with a senior in their lives.”

item.title: Statement from Minister Jenn Redmond on Women’s History Month
item.description:
Statement from Minister Jenn Redmond on Women’s History Month jenniferdhogan Thu, 10/01/2026 - 09:36

Today, Minister Jenn Redmond, Minister responsible for the status of women issued the following statement recognizing October as Women’s History Month: 

“October is Women’s History Month in Canada, a time to reflect on the women and girls who have helped shape our communities, our province, and our country.

Every day, women make a difference. They lead businesses, care for families, strengthen workplaces, support their neighbours, and volunteer in their communities. Many of these contributions take place quietly, without recognition, but they matter deeply.

This month is an opportunity to celebrate the achievements of women from all walks of life. It is also a chance to encourage the next generation of women and girls to pursue their goals, share their talents, and follow their own path with confidence.

Across Prince Edward Island, we are fortunate to be surrounded by women who inspire us through their leadership, kindness, and commitment to making our communities better places to live.

During Women’s History Month, I encourage all Islanders to take a moment to recognize the women who have influenced their lives, whether they are family members, friends, colleagues, mentors, or community leaders.”

item.title: Province marks National Day for Truth and Reconciliation
item.description:
Province marks National Day for Truth and Reconciliation jenniferdhogan Wed, 09/30/2026 - 12:47

Today, September 30, is the National Day for Truth and Reconciliation, a time to recognize the lasting impacts of the residential school system and to honour the survivors, the children who never returned home, and their families and communities.

Also recognized as Orange Shirt Day, the day provides an opportunity to reflect on the history and legacy of residential schools and the ongoing work toward reconciliation. 

Islanders are encouraged to wear orange in recognition of the message that Every Child Matters and to learn more about the history and ongoing impacts of residential schools.

To mark the day, Premier Rob Lantz invited the Chiefs of the PEI Mi’kmaq First Nations, along with members of the Indigenous community and the public, for a short reflection at the Provincial Administration Building this morning. Flags were lowered to half-mast following the gathering.

The Provincial Administration Building will be lit in orange this evening.

Quotes:  

“On the sixth annual observance of the National Day for Truth and Reconciliation, also known as Orange Shirt Day, Epekwitk (Prince Edward Island) joins the rest of Canada to honour the generations of Indigenous children who were forced to attend residential schools, day schools, and related institutions, and in remembering and mourning all those who died or disappeared and never returned home. This solemn occasion provides us all with an opportunity not just to listen and learn, but also to act. On September 30, and every day after, we must stand in steadfast solidarity with the Indigenous families and communities who continue to carry the impacts of this history and legacy, and walk alongside them on the long journey toward reconciliation rooted in truth, driven by justice, and sustained through healing." 

-Senator Brian Francis 

“It is easy to become lost in the sorrow and trauma of Residential School Survivors' experiences, and in the holes left in our families and communities by the children who did not return. It would be so easy to give up. Instead, our communities stood up. The strength, resilience, and kindness I see daily among the Mi'kmaq bolsters my spirit. I have hope and faith for our future, one where Mi'kmaw culture is honoured and Mi'kmaw children know their ancestors and traditions.”

- Lennox Island First Nation Chief Tabatha Bernard

“Coming together today to reflect on truth and reconciliation reminds us that healing is a journey we walk together. We remember the children, and we honour the strength of Survivors and their families. That strength is carried forward by each generation, and intergenerational healing grows when we learn from one another, listen with open hearts, and share our stories with our children and grandchildren. When Mi'kmaq and Islanders work side by side, we build a future rooted in understanding, respect, and pride in who we are.”  

- Abegweit First Nation Chief Junior Gould

“Reconciliation is a responsibility we share and it requires us to listen, learn and act. Today, we remember the children who never came home, honour survivors and their families, and recognize the lasting impacts of residential schools. Our government is committed to continuing this work alongside First Nations and Indigenous communities, strengthening relationships built on respect, trust and a shared commitment to reconciliation.” 

-Premier Rob Lantz

Learn more about National Day for Truth and Reconciliation.

item.title: Feedback wanted on changes to Consumer Reporting Act
item.description:
Feedback wanted on changes to Consumer Reporting Act ddgillis Tue, 09/29/2026 - 13:48

The province is inviting residents and interested stakeholders to share their feedback on laws affecting consumer reporting agencies.

The proposed amendments would remove the requirement for a consumer reporting agency, such as a credit bureau, to maintain a fixed place of business in PEI and would make related changes to support regulatory oversight. The changes would also allow consumers to request and receive a consumer report by telephone, mail or electronically.

“While consumer reporting agencies have traditionally maintained offices in PEI, this is not always possible. We need a mechanism that better reflects how consumers access this service today and aligns with regulatory approaches in the other provinces. The proposed changes will ensure PEI residents can access their consumer report by telephone, mail or electronically, which will bring us in alignment with the rules in most other Canadian provinces.”

- Justice and Public Safety Minister Bloyce Thompson

Consultation documents are available at Department of Justice and Public Safety Public Consultations for people to review. 

Comments in English or French for all documents can be submitted by email to justicepolicy@gov.pe.ca until October 15, 2026.

item.title: Premier McLeod on the Enbridge Line 21 Pipeline
item.description:
YELLOWKNIFE - Premier Bob McLeod issued the following statement on the Enbridge Line 21 pipeline today:

“I was pleased to learn that operations have resumed for Enbridge’s Line 21 pipeline after almost 2 years of no activity.

"Resource development has, and will continue to be, the backbone of our economy and is central to ensuring a good source of middle class jobs and business opportunities. Our territory has mineral and petroleum resources and the development of those resources can have a transformative effect on our people and economy.

"Sustainable economic development is key to the future of Northerners. With a strong resource development base, we will be able to support diversification of our local economies into emerging and established sectors.

"On behalf of the Government of the Northwest Territories I’d like to offer my congratulations to Imperial Oil, Enbridge the town of Norman Wells and other partners for getting this pipeline back up and running. I know the efforts and economic impacts of the pipeline have already begun to take shape in the community and will be felt for years to come. ”

 

Charlotte Digness
Media and Communications Coordinator
Cabinet Communications and Protocol
Government of the Northwest Territories
